page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v6 is a virtual machine variant tailored for compute-biased workloads requiring direct high-speed local disk access. Based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance is powered by a dedicated 16-vCPU, 8-physical-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache along with advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector acceleration. It comes equipped with 32 GB of memory, representing an allocation of 2 GB per vCPU, and integrates a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD for fast temporary scratch space.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate standout single-threaded execution and localized compute processing. The platform scored 2163 in Geekbench single-core testing and achieved 31.37 GB/s in single-threaded gzip compression, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Furthermore, text generation on small language models reached 396.44 tokens per second, securing a top-decile rating. General multi-core tests, including PassMark CPU (26706.63) and Geekbench multi-core (13256), perform steadily within the median tier, as do memory-bound operations such as uncached block reads (125.11 GB/s) and writes (71.18 GB/s).

By pairing 16 vCPUs with 32 GB of RAM, the instance adopts a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, prioritizing raw processing capacity and local storage over large memory footprints. This architectural profile offers operational cost efficiency for CPU-dominant applications that do not require standard 1:4 memory allocations, avoiding payment for idle RAM. The primary tradeoff is the memory constraint, which limits in-memory database scaling or massive caching architectures. Consequently, the D16lds_v6 is well aligned for CI/CD compilation pipelines, web application serving, batch ETL processing, small-scale AI inference, and tasks benefiting from fast ephemeral NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v6 is a compute-aligned virtual machine configuration within the general-purpose D-series, configured with a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It is powered by a dedicated 16-vCPU, 8-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, complete with Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server includes 32 GB of system memory (2 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 945 GB NVMe solid-state drive for local scratch and caching needs. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core capabilities, registering top-quartile performance in Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, alongside top-decile text generation throughput in small language models. Its multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth align with mid-range tiers. The lower memory footprint relative to CPU cores yields cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not demand extensive RAM pools, such as CI/CD compilation, stateless web processing, batch ETL jobs, and local disk-intensive tasks.
